items.title: SPHMC stationary phase-reference moments

source.anchor: Section 3.1 definition of pi_eta and Pi_eta; Lemma D.4 proof after equation (D.3)
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS supplies the omitted independent-Gaussian and product-integral details.

items.statement: For pi_eta=pi*N(0,eta I) and Pi_eta=pi_eta tensor N(0,I), the stationary reference law has explicit finite position and momentum second moments; ASTIS proves the generic standard-deviation-scale identity used by this specialization.
assumptions: A probability base law with an integrable, bounded position second moment.
Use sigma=sqrt eta to recover the paper's variance parameter eta.

obligations.label: Insert the compiled Gibbs moment and sigma=sqrt eta (remaining integration)

bindings.boundary: Generic smoothing identity only; no phase dynamics.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper defines pi_eta using covariance eta I.
assumption_deltas.lean: The theorem accepts every real standard-deviation scale sigma and produces covariance sigma^2 I.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source is recovered by sigma=sqrt eta under eta>=0; sign is immaterial because the second moment depends on sigma squared.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper works with its strongly log-concave Gibbs target.
assumption_deltas.lean: The identity holds for any probability law with the displayed finite position second moment.
assumption_deltas.reason: No Gibbs structure is used in the independent-noise calculation.

bindings.boundary: Reference moments only; D.3, history, D.7 and D.8 remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper writes Pi_eta=pi_eta tensor N(0,I) and later uses its moments inside universal constants.
assumption_deltas.lean: ASTIS constructs the actual product measure and states probability, coordinate integrability, exact coordinate integrals and the explicit combined bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: These facts are required before the later transport-to-moment and Fubini steps are valid.

assumption_deltas.source: Strong convexity supplies the base Gibbs position moment.
assumption_deltas.lean: This bounded packet takes the base moment M as an explicit premise.
assumption_deltas.reason: The already compiled Gibbs moment is kept as a separate parent; its final specialization remains a visible integration edge.
